## Summary

A strategy tweet in the classic seasonal-tendency shape: **short NQ futures every Monday when Friday's high was never broken**, backtested on real tick data Feb 2022–May 2026. Claimed: **+573.30% return, PF 2.96, win rate 22.6%** (wins less than 1 in 4), **avg R:R 10.13, max DD −15.2%**. Total trades truncated.

## Why it matters

- **This is the exact genre Peter warns about** — the quoted tweet in [[2026-10-01-dmartin-hypothesis-first]] (same week, same ecosystem): "find the right weekday, hour and filter, get a nice backtest, call it an edge… I'm skeptical even when it stays profitable out of sample." A weekday-gated NQ short with a 10:1 average R:R is either a genuine gap-risk premium or a curve-fit to a handful of Monday crashes; the 22.6% win rate means the whole return rides on few fat tails.
- **Sample-size math is the first check:** with wins <1-in-4 and avg R:R 10, +573% over ~4.25 years implies the edge concentrates in a small number of outsized Monday winners — remove the top 2–3 and the system likely flatlines. The truncated total-trade count is the key missing number.
- **Skepticism gates:** no economic mechanism stated (why would unbroken Friday high predict Monday downside?); no out-of-sample split disclosed; "real tick data" ≠ walk-forward; photo unopened. Capture as a stress-test case for our seasonal-skepticism checklist, not a replication candidate.
